The "no anticholinergic burden" advantage is the single most important comparison point versus antimuscarinics — make sure students can articulate why that specifically matters in an older adult population.
Reinforce that these are complementary, not competing, mechanisms — this is the mechanistic basis for combination therapy mentioned on the previous slide.

The Unit 5 cross-reference here is deliberate and worth stating explicitly — tamsulosin and doxazosin are not new drug classes, they are the same alpha1-blocker pharmacology applied to a different primary indication.
Tamsulosin and silodosin are uroselective; doxazosin and terazosin lower BP more.

Same receptor family as in blood vessels.
